classification_reasons: Blast radius is large by file count (107 files in the merge-base...HEAD diff: HANDOFF.md, README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, the two stubs, 30 docs/notes/<N>.md, 26 docs/decisions/<N>.md, 21 docs/progress/<...>.md plus three index.md, this change's own evidence/status files), even though no plugin/, template/ or tests/ file is touched and no risk_list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) is implicated, so 'few files' does not hold.

No existing automated test exercises this diff, and none is expected to (docs-only, nothing in plugin/ reads these files at runtime per plan.md's own grep-confirmed finding); acceptance is a human/verifier link-resolution pass over ~140 citations, not pytest coverage.

The spec itself is unusually tight for everything it does cover (every Requirement has a decided answer, both Flagged concerns closed with a recorded decision, acceptance is mechanically checkable), but the plan's own Risks section documents real uncertainty baked into the design (the exact file count was unknown until phase (c) ran, because sessions 15-18 kept appending to the three source docs between spec time and build time) - exactly the kind of surface area that benefits from a human read rather than being waved through as routine.
attempted: Intent: re-read intent.md's problem and Proposed outcome from scratch and compared against spec.md, plan.md and the diff; the delivered split (docs/notes/, docs/decisions/, docs/progress/ each with an index.md, two stubs, the four named live-doc link updates, the CLAUDE.md edit table left for the owner in docs/PROGRESS.md) matches the stated intent, including the deliberate exclusions (docs/BUILD_GUIDE.md, docs/MODEL_ALLOCATION.md, the historical docs under docs/handoffs|reviews|proposals).

Spec and plan: checked spec.md Requirements/Design and every plan.md Order-of-work step against the diff's actual files; sampled docs/notes/1.md and docs/notes/11.md (11a/11b/11c stay inside the parent file), docs/decisions/18.md (status: amended, amended_by: 21, matching the source's own amendment text) and docs/decisions/index.md (ascending number order, one line per decision) and docs/progress/index.md (ascending session order, the non-session records placed by date, 21 archived files matching the plan's build-time-derived count rather than the spec's stale '14', exactly as plan.md's Risks section said would happen). Both Flagged concerns in spec.md are closed with a recorded decision, not left open. plan_sync (gate-c.json, prior round) reports every committed file is in plan.md.

Proof: build.log/test.log/lint.log all carry the deferred-to-the-runner header (CI session, plugin 0.3.2 mechanism) and the prior completed gate-b.json run they point back to was green (1391 passed, ruff clean) - not a claim, a prior toolchain run; verifier.md reports a detailed, itemised exercise of the changed behaviour (index completeness by file count, citation resolution sampled across ~15 call sites, guardrail/scope diff check) and a 'matches the plan' verdict with no mismatch found.

Blast radius: confirmed via the diff's own --stat (107 files, all under docs/, HANDOFF.md, README.md and this change's evidence/status.yaml - nothing under plugin/, template/ or tests/); grepped the whole diff for '.env' / 'fixtures/sample-python-project' and found only prose discussion inside docs/notes and docs/progress content (the NOTES §27/§30/§31/§32 narrative about issue #91 and this very park), never an actual change to the fixture file - the clean_tree park the owner dismissed is confirmed not to be part of this diff. hook-log.jsonl has zero deny entries. Compared the blob hash of docs/notes/1.md across the diff's three nested self-referential copies (3f47020 every time): this fix round changed no content, only evidence/status files, consistent with the stated 'no code changes' scope.

Policies: security-baseline/data-conventions not implicated (no secret or PII, text is pre-existing platform facts/decisions/session records moved verbatim, per spec.md's own rule-by-rule statement); ux-conventions inapplicable (no UI). REVIEW.md's Important criteria checked: no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) touched; change_type is feature, not fix, so the test-file-lock rule does not apply; plan.md matches the diff; CLAUDE.md's now-outdated references are handed to the owner as the required table rather than edited in-session.
Tests: no behavior changed (docs-only, confirmed no plugin/template/tests file in the diff), so no test could pass with a bug present or be weakened - there is no code path for a bug to hide in.
